country.comment: Empirical investigation conducted in the urban district (Amphoe Muang) of Pathumthani province in the Bangkok Metropolitan Region, Thailand.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1.1; PDF p. 12, Section 4.2

effect_estimate.comment: Pre-post (1998 vs. 2003) chi-squared comparisons of household survey data and PWA municipal administrative/technical records.
effect_estimate.value: Following the 1998 Pathumthani BOOT water supply privatisation (where PWA retained retail billing and progressive cross-subsidised national tariffs while contracting bulk production, network expansion, and maintenance to PTW), household metered piped water access in informal settlements rose from 28.0% in 1998 to 84.0% in 2003 (+56.0 percentage points, chi-squared = 47.727, p < 0.01), including increases from 11.8% to 85.3% (+73.5 pp, chi-squared = 36.796, p < 0.01) in small informal settlements and from 41.5% to 82.9% (+41.4 pp, chi-squared = 14.989, p < 0.01) in large informal settlements, outpacing formal communities (76.8% to 93.9%, +17.1 pp, chi-squared = 11.675, p < 0.01). Income-poor households (<=7,500 baht/month) saw piped access increase from 50.0% to 88.6% (+38.6 pp, chi-squared = 15.441, p < 0.01) vs. 57.7% to 90.0% (+32.3 pp, chi-squared = 35.128, p < 0.01) among income-non-poor households, while total PWA municipal household connections increased by 58.03% from 15,495 to 24,488. Informal-community households reported significant improvements in water clarity (+26.8 pp, chi-squared = 12.041, p < 0.01), drinkability (+14.7 pp, chi-squared = 4.086, p < 0.05), turbidity (+15.8 pp, chi-squared = 3.590, p < 0.10), 24-hour reliability (+12.6 pp, chi-squared = 3.384, p < 0.10), adequate pressure (+35.0 pp, chi-squared = 19.180, p < 0.01; PWA technical data: 2.4 to 4.0 bars), and same-day complaint response (+54.8 pp, chi-squared = 15.033, p < 0.01; PWA response time: 60-120 min to 15 min). Costs rose for a subset of informal-settlement households: the share paying <=2,000 baht for connection fell from 75.0% to 51.7% (-23.3 pp, chi-squared = 3.316, p < 0.10) and the share paying <=375 baht/month fell from 95.5% to 74.0% (-21.5 pp, chi-squared = 4.693, p < 0.05), though changes among income-poor households were not statistically significant (+1.5 pp for connection cost, chi-squared = 0.009; -16.1 pp for monthly charge, chi-squared = 1.455).
